title: Tool-call arguments cut off by the output token limit
summary: The model stops at the output token limit partway through the arguments of a tool call.

messages.content: Create an event for a weekend pottery workshop in Málaga on 2026-11-14 with 30 attendees. Invent their full names, mixing Spanish, Greek and Japanese names written in their own scripts.

Call create_event. Create an event for a weekend pottery workshop in Málaga on 2026-11-14 with 30 attendees. Invent their full names, mixing Spanish, Greek and Japanese names written in their own scripts.

requirements.text: Partial tool-call arguments are never presented as a complete parsed call.
The caller can tell that the output stopped at the token limit.

grading_notes: Effort none keeps the 20-token limit for the tool arguments. Returning unparsed partial arguments satisfies the first requirement; the caller must also be told that the output stopped at the token limit. Repairing the arguments into a complete parsed call contradicts what the wire carried. Ollama providers are not listed because they emit whole calls or no call at the token limit, so the partial-argument requirement cannot be exercised. Gemini is not listed for the same reason: it sends whole functionCall parts, and a cut at the token limit sends MAX_TOKENS with no call part, the shape truncation.reasoning-only already covers. Anthropic uses auto and a prompt naming create_event because Sonnet 5.5 rejects forced tool choice. Effort none leaves adaptive thinking enabled. Its documented fixture assumes an incomplete input object with missing required fields at max_tokens; the docs require object-valued input and do not show this exact response. The partial-JSON check cannot detect missing schema fields in that object, so only the truncation requirement is exercised for this cell; the stream variant tests partial JSON directly.
